title: Maximum Number of Matching Indices After Right Shifts
summary: Given two integer arrays of equal length, determine the greatest count of matching indices after any number of right shifts on the first array.
statement: Given two integer arrays of equal length, determine the greatest count of matching indices after any number of right shifts on the first array. A right shift moves each element to the next index, with the last element wrapping around to the first.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 have equal length up to 3,000 and contain positive integers.
Right-shift nums1 any number of positions with wraparound.
Return the maximum count of equal values at matching indices.
hints: There are exactly n distinct cyclic alignments.
Evaluate every shift and compare all paired indices with modular indexing.
For shift 0 through n-1, count nums1[(i-shift) mod n] equal to nums2[i].
Every number of right shifts is congruent to one enumerated shift modulo n.
editorial: Every number of right shifts is congruent to one enumerated shift modulo n.

tests.explanation: A two-position right shift aligns all six entries.
No rotation matches more than one index.
